items.name: theme
items.title: agentui theme
items.description: Graphite: shadcn/ui's neutral theme in the system's fonts (the platform's UI and monospace faces, not Geist, then its faces for Chinese, Japanese and Korean: PingFang SC, Hiragino Sans and Apple SD Gothic Neo on Apple's, Microsoft YaHei, Yu Gothic UI and Malgun Gothic on Windows, Noto Sans CJK elsewhere), drawn antialiased, a quarter em between CJK and Latin letters or digits (text-autospace, not in code), with a third, fainter text grey (`subtle-foreground`, `text-subtle-foreground`: placeholders, counts, times, labels, set at 4.5:1 or more on the background, cards, popovers and the sidebar), for base-nova in pure greys (no accent colour, a darker sidebar under an inset page in dark), with WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (but for text fields' edges: a lighter `field` grey, border-field, for Input, Textarea, Select, InputGroup and the like, their focus a bright edge and ring; checkboxes, radios and switches keep `input`, 3:1), success, warning and info colours, distinguishable chart colours, Windows high contrast support, native controls and scrollbars in the current colour scheme, a hairline lift for what is selected on a grey ground (shadow-raised: the active tab, the rail's current area), a soft shadow for what floats (shadow-float, and shadcn's shadow-md and shadow-lg: the composer, menus, popovers, find bars, toasts) and a deeper one under dialogs over a darker overlay in dark, grey menu icons and text selection, dimmed disabled accordion and radio items, icon lines 1.5px at any size (an outline icon whose paths carry their own stroke, as Hugeicons' do), a shimmer whose band is seen on any text it sweeps, in either theme: toward stronger contrast, or on text already at the text's colour away from it (shadcn's fades text almost into a light background; its band, and this theme's before, could not be seen on the text's own colour), paused out of view where an element carries `data-shimmer-paused` (use-shimmer-pause sets it), scroll fades that do not restyle a scrolling element's content as it scrolls, and a type scale of named steps (text-2xs 11px, text-2sm 13px, text-md 15px, text-display 22px for a page's one heading, text-readout 32px for a short code read out, with their line heights) rounded-xs on the radius ladder (4px) and rounded-composer (16px, the composer's box), so that components use no pixel values of their own, `touch-target`, a positioned element's place 44px at least where the pointer is a finger (`pointer: coarse`), syntax colours for code (--code-keyword, --code-string, --code-number, --code-function, --code-type, --code-tag, --code-property, --code-comment and their code-* classes, 4.5:1 or more where code is shown, greys under [data-code-tone=graphite]), and a moment's mark (animate-highlight: the accent fading out over 1.2s, for a message the reader was taken to), a height a share of the window's (max-h-dvh-60: 60dvh, for what scrolls in itself, as a long card, with overflow-y-auto and tabIndex={0} for the keyboard), one timing for motion, by name (motion-hover 100ms for a row's background as the pointer comes, given to menu, select, combobox, command and composer-select items; motion-fade 150ms; motion-size 200ms; motion-slide 400ms for a sheet, a drawer, a toast; motion-pop for a popup, in at 150ms on --ease-enter and out at 100ms on --ease-exit; four curves: --ease-ui in place, --ease-enter, --ease-exit and --ease-slide, a finger's sheet; Tailwind's bare transitions and its ease-out, ease-in and ease-in-out are the theme's, and the accordion's), a loading state seen only past a wait (animate-wait-in: unseen for --motion-wait, 300ms, then faded in), a skeleton's pulse on --motion-pulse (2s) and --ease-loop, none where the reader asks for less motion (the pulse stopped too, the wait kept); room for what covers the window's edges (pb-safe, pb-safe-or-<n>, bottom-safe-offset-<n> for the home indicator; pt-safe-or-<n>, top-safe-offset-<n> for AgentApp's titlebar or the status bar), grid-cols-icon and grid-cols-icon-end (a 16px icon's column, the rest and an end), --line-mark (1.5px, the line that marks: icons' strokes, a selected cell's edge), bg-checkerboard and bg-dot-grid. An app's palette sets seven base roles (background, foreground, primary, accent, sidebar, border, ring) on :root in a CSS file of its own; the rest are derived from them. `frame` (bg-frame) is the window's colour around an AgentApp's card, its titlebar and rail: in light a step darker than the sidebar (4% of the text's into it, as a desktop app's chrome), muted text 4.5:1 on it; in dark the sidebar's. html is painted in the background, for a native shell to follow. short: is a named variant for a screen under 30rem tall (a phone on its side), as a drawer's footer uses. ::highlight(mark) and ::highlight(mark-current) are named CSS Custom Highlights, a search's matches and the one it is at, in --mark and --mark-current (a highlight of a component's own name takes those colours). shadow-mark-start marks a current row at its start edge (--line-mark, in the text's colour); shadow-rule rules a bar off below without taking room. With a Window Controls Overlay (the app's <html data-window-controls-overlay>, or a PWA's display-mode) and no AgentApp titlebar, the window's own buttons keep their place: a sidebar's header and the rail start under env(titlebar-area-height), the sidebar's bar and a header at the window's edge start past env(titlebar-area-x), the sidebar's edge rail and the skip link under them.

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova code-block, fixed: the copy button takes labels for its name and its announcement, for other languages, says copied only while the value is the one copied, and says it could not copy when the clipboard refuses or the page has none (plain http, not a secure context) instead of throwing, output that streams in costs its new lines, not every line, to render and lay out (numbered too: blocks with the numbers in a gutter, not a grid of every line), a removed line's tint leaves coloured code (GitHub's red keywords) at 4.5:1, a diff is in greys (added lines a light grey with their +, removed ones struck through in the faintest grey on no tint, with their −), a line takes its own `number` (a diff's line in its file), code is 12px on 20px lines (an interface at 13px reads it so, not at the prose's 14px) and highlighted lines and pressed toggles show on the dark surface, the block has a hairline border and a card's corners, its header is a 36px bar over a divider with the title in grey mono, line numbers are a step lighter, in a gutter at least `--code-block-gutter-min` wide (24px by default), the copy button floating over the code is raised by shadow-float, the destructive block (failed output) is told in greys by weight, its text and title heavier, not red, the header's buttons and toggles are one size, the content fades at the edges it scrolls past, down as well as sideways, and is translate="no", so a page translator leaves code and output as written. With `lines`, a block longer than that folds in its own card: those lines whole (a wrapped line counts each it takes, a diff's @@ lines are not counted), its last two fading out, and a bar across its foot inside its border, "Show all · 30 lines", that shows the rest; open, the bar folds it again, and its header sticks to the top of what scrolls with a button that folds it, the block's start kept in view. Its words are `labels` (more, less, lines, collapse); `open`, `defaultOpen` and `onOpenChange` control it. Lines are measured after layout by one ResizeObserver, only those up to the fold, so output streaming in stays cheap; focus or find in the page reaching the folded part opens it; copying copies it all. The lines past the fold can be one plain text (CodeBlockRest; CodeBlockContent's own text does it), hidden until found, so a folded block of thousands of lines costs the dozen it shows and find in the page still opens it; open, they become lines 250 at a time as they near the view, each where its text was, the text laid out only near the view (useCodeBlockCut and cutLines for the app's own lines). The block clips rather than hides its overflow, so the header can stick. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: combobox
items.title: Combobox
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova combobox, fixed: Names the icon-only trigger, clear and chip remove buttons, and takes the input's trigger out of the tab order. Items can show a checkbox before them (indicator="checkbox"), for choosing many. Its input is Base UI's input group, so the list lines up with the whole field, an icon before the input included. The theme's shadow-md and shadow-lg are shadow-float, so its popup drops shadcn's ring, which doubled the shadow's hairline; an input in its popup is the page's colour inside a hairline, as a search field is drawn (the input grey for both fill and border drew a darker rim); its rows are 32px tall (min-h-8) with an 8px radius, as in every menu. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md). It pops in and out by the theme's motion-pop (in at 150ms on --ease-enter, out at 100ms on --ease-exit), not shadcn's 100ms on `ease`.

items.name: command
items.title: Command
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova command, fixed: Renders the separator as a presentational rule, since a listbox may only contain options and groups. Its rows are 32px tall (min-h-8) with an 8px radius, as in every menu. Its input is the page's colour inside a hairline, as a search field is drawn (the input grey for both its fill and its border drew a darker rim, like an inset shadow). Its value is always controlled inside (`value`, or `defaultValue`, with `onValueChange` called either way): the arrows scroll the highlighted option into view and make it the input's aria-activedescendant even when the options don't render again (memoized, or compiled by the React Compiler); the active descendant is named on mount, for a value the app sets and when the options are rendered anew; and mounted with a query, the value given stays highlighted until the reader acts, where cmdk would highlight the first hit. CommandDialog size="fixed" is 32rem tall and centred whatever its results; size="wide" the same at 42rem wide, for a palette of groups and shortcuts. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: context-menu
items.title: Context Menu
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova context-menu, fixed: The theme's shadow-md and shadow-lg are shadow-float, so its popup drops shadcn's ring, which doubled the shadow's hairline; its rows are 32px tall (min-h-8) with an 8px radius, as in every menu. On a phone (narrower than 640px) a long press opens it as a sheet from the bottom, as the platform's action sheets do: across the screen over a scrim that closes it when tapped, a handle to swipe it down by, its rows 44px tall, clear of the home indicator, and `sheetTitle` on top; it stays Base UI's popup, its roles, focus and keys. `sheet={false}` keeps it anchored. items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova dialog, fixed: the close buttons take closeLabel, their name for other languages, where "Close" was written in. No taller than the window (the theme's, 1rem from its edges, for AlertDialog too); DialogBody is what scrolls between its header and footer, keyboard-reachable while it scrolls. Its footer's buttons sit under the content, without shadcn's ruled-off band (a stray line in dark, where the band hardly shows). DialogContent size="wide": a picker's (a list and a view), 768px wide and 640px tall whatever it shows, no taller than the window, on a phone the whole screen clear of the home indicator. It pops in and out by the theme's motion-pop (in at 150ms on --ease-enter, out at 100ms on --ease-exit), not shadcn's 100ms on `ease`. DialogContent takes size="full" too, for a reader or a viewer over the app: the window but for 32px round it (a className's max width or height keeps it centred), on a phone the whole screen. On a phone (under 640px) a default-size DialogContent is a sheet from the bottom: the screen's width, its top corners round, at most 90% of the screen, clear of the home indicator, sliding; it scrolls whole, its title with it (sheet={false} where it places itself). A default-size one's footer, the content's last, stays at its foot as the rest scrolls under it (a wide or full one's is laid out there), and on a short screen (short:) its buttons are in a row. The close button is 32px, 8px in, on the title's middle line, and the title keeps clear of it.

items.title: Sheet
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova sheet, fixed: the close button takes closeLabel, its name for other languages, where "Close" was written in; its overlay is a flat scrim (20% black), not a blur. It slides by the theme's motion-slide (400ms on --ease-slide, the platform's sheet curve), its overlay with it.

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova toast, fixed: A dialog's radius (rounded-xl, not 2xl) and no border: shadow-lg is the theme's shadow-float, which has its own hairline. Toaster takes position (bottom-end, or top-end under AgentApp's titlebar and the status bar), --toast-inset-end on the root to keep clear of the window's end, and pinned, a card that stays where the toasts show. It moves by the theme's motion-slide on --ease-enter, its height by motion-fade.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova tooltip, fixed: 24px tall with a 6px radius and no arrow, its words 11px (text-2xs), a small label as agentui's floating things are. On its inverted surface, secondary text (text-muted-foreground, text-subtle-foreground: a FieldDescription's) is the background's colour faded, legible. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md). It pops in and out by the theme's motion-pop (in at 150ms on --ease-enter, out at 100ms on --ease-exit), not shadcn's 100ms on `ease`.

items.name: sidebar
items.title: Sidebar
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova sidebar, fixed: SidebarProvider takes `sheet`, which makes the sidebar a sheet wider than a phone too, where the page has no room for it beside the main area, and Sidebar takes `sheetClassName` for that sheet (agent-app folds its sidebar so on a tablet or an unfolded phone, and opens it past its rail); it is a sheet below 640px, not 768px (Tailwind's `sm`, as use-mobile's), its actions' larger hit areas and always-shown hover actions follow a touch screen (`pointer: coarse`), not the width, and its content scrolls only up and down, so those hit areas past its edge don't let a finger swipe it sideways. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md). It folds by the theme's motion-size on --ease-ui, not 200ms linear.

items.name: agent-event
items.title: Agent Event
items.description: What came to the agent from outside, neither the reader nor the agent speaking: a line of a stream it watches (kind monitor), a background task's end (task), a wake-up it had set (wake). One light grey pill at the conversation's start edge, as wide as it needs, 28px high (36px on a phone): its kind's icon, its source (the kind's word or the app's source), what it said cut short (whole on hover), when (time). With details (a task's report) it is a button opening the report under it in a bordered box that scrolls past 24rem, meta (what it cost, e.g. "12 tool uses · 3m 20s") at its foot, else at the line's end; status failed or stopped says so after its words, an alert or a stop before them, by weight, not a colour. In an AgentTurn it is a part ({ type: "event" }) where it came, never folded into a run of steps, events in a row close together; between turns, rendered itself. foldKey keeps it opened under a FoldProvider; its words are labels (in a turn, its labels.event, a part's own labels over them).

items.name: agent-turn
items.title: Agent Turn
items.description: An agent's turn in a conversation: its reasoning and tool calls, and what it said in between, under one title ("Worked for 6m 12s") above its answer, its chevron after it and a rule under it when open. Each step is a line of what was done, not what was typed: an icon for its kind (a book for a read, a pencil for an edit, a terminal for a command), its verb and what it acted on a step lighter (files by their names, underlined with dots, the path on hover), what came of it at the end ("4 edits · +38 −12", an alert and "Exit 2" by weight, not red) and how long it took on hover. A call's kind (read, search, list, edit, write, command, or the app's own) and its data (command, description, path, pattern, added and removed lines, diff, output, exit code) are enough: describeCommand reads a shell command as a read ("Read composer.tsx", "Read 3 files"), a search, a listing or an edit (sed -i), else a short command as it is ("Ran pnpm build"), else the agent's own description, as it is, the same while it runs and once done, else "Ran a script"; a leading cd is left out. A run, the steps between two things it said, is one row a thing: a file's edits merged (opened, their hunks by the file's order with their new line numbers, the first lines and "Show all"), files written in a row on one row, reads, searches and listings in a row under one nested line ("Read 6 files, searched 3 times"); it folds under one line past three kinds keeping edits, commands and reads first, the rest counted ("Explored 6 files, edited 4, ran 4 commands and 6 other actions"), files once each, and at its end the failures nothing later made good (on a phone the number alone). A command opened shows itself whole, wrapped, to copy (and to open in the app's view with onExpand), and its output's last lines on the side's grey, the earlier ones on request, each line in its tone: what failed strong, the output muted, passes and the tally faint (agentOutputTone, or the app's outputTone). While it runs nothing opens or closes by itself: the live run is one line, saying the step a tool is at in place of its sum, each step's in turn as they come, as a GPT turn does (a spinner, shimmering; opened, its sum and the step under way under the list; a step waiting for the reader, with a progress line or media, or opened by the reader stands under it; a shield and "Wants to run …", "Waiting for you" while it waits for the reader); what the reader opened stays open and new steps join it; the turn folds once, when it ends, only if the reader never touched it, so the answer does not move. Folded, a failure nothing made good is still seen at its title's end ("1 failed", an alert before it). Stopped or failed, its title says so ("Stopped after 2m 03s") and its last row where ("Stopped while running Type-check the app"); stopped, what it had said is kept, dimmed, and under it its whole footer, its facts how it ended ("Stopped by you · 12:06"), so retry is a press away. While it runs and the app's link to the agent is lost, connection says so at its end, a status ("Reconnecting 2/5" shimmering, or "Disconnected"), in place of its spinner. While it runs, its title is in the text's colour, shimmering, as a running step's words are; while it thinks, it says so ("Thinking · 4s") over a running step's spinner and the thought's newest bold heading, else its newest paragraph's first sentence, with Markdown stripped, muted, so it is seen going; once over, a quiet line ("Thought for 12s"), with no title over it when it is all the work; while it only thinks, its title is bare, its chevron and rule shown in their places when a step comes. While it runs, its title counts the time since startedAt each second and shows the app's metrics ("Working · 47s · 38 tok/s"); between steps, when nothing else is seen going, its end has a spinner alone, in the place an AgentTurnFooter then takes. A subagent is a step whose details are its own AgentTurn, its steps listed as they came one level under its words, with no run's line over them (its words are that line) and no title of its own and what it handed back last (AgentTurnResult, cut to 6 lines over "Show all" where long). AgentTurnStep is a call's line alone, outside a turn. AgentTurnTarget with href is a link on its step's line, over the line's button, shimmering itself while the step runs (in WebKit, a link's own layer gets none of its words' shimmer); in a fold's line, a button, it is its words alone. All its words are labels, for other languages. The reader's choices are kept with use-fold. Under an ended turn, its footer: copy, retry with a menu of other ways, the app's actions and a menu of more on the left; the model, how long and when on the right, a fact saying more alone on hover (AgentTurnFact: the time's full date), the turn's numbers in a card when pressed, in groups under their labels; its menus' hints plain small text, retry's menu opened from the whole retry group. Its actions shown on hover for turns before the last, its facts always; a finger's size on a phone; an open run's list (or a run of reads alone, opened) scrolls past min(18rem, 50dvh), fading at its edges and growing by the steps the reader opened in it, with the live step outside it, and while it runs it opens at its newest steps and follows them as they come unless the reader scrolled up; a command's output says "Earlier output not shown" or "Later output not shown" where the source cut it (outputTruncated: "start" or "end"), "No output" when a finished command printed nothing and "Loading output…" while outputLoading, and shown whole it scrolls past 20rem and follows its end while it runs unless the reader scrolled up; steps and onLoadSteps let a turn's steps load when opened, with three skeleton lines or a message and Retry. Toggling a fold keeps its line in place on screen, except while the conversation follows its live end. What the reader decided (a decision's row) and what a step viewed or made (its `media`, e.g. thumbnails, shown under its line) stay in sight right after a folded run's line or the folded work's title, in order (side by side, each picture's card as wide as alone in the conversation, up to 6 of the 12 columns; a step's several pictures or a video a row of their own), and show once, in place, when opened; a step still under way does too under an ended turn's folded work. What came from outside (an event part, an AgentEvent: a monitor's line, a background task's end, a wake-up) stays where it came, never folded into a run, one after the last step with the answer. What the user sent while it ran (a steer part) stays where it came, at its end edge as the user's message (UserMessageText's bubble and 16px text, cut to 6 lines over "Show all" where long), always seen, and the work before and after it each fold under a title as a turn's work, with its own time ("Worked for 40s"; the last "Working" while it runs, counted from its steer), steers back to back splitting it once; an attempt cut off and replaced (a superseded part) is one closed line ("Superseded attempt · Cut off by a steer") that opens to its parts, loaded when opened if they are not there yet. While a ConversationFind is open, each closed fold (work, run, step, superseded attempt, a command's earlier output lines) holds its text, read from the parts' data, hidden until found (FoldFindText); found, it opens as if the reader had opened it, its content not mounted until then.

items.name: agent-turn-changes
items.title: Agent Turn Changes
items.description: What a turn changed and drew on, under its answer once the turn has ended. AgentTurnChanges: a 1.5px dotted border-colour rule with 16px above and below separates the answer from the card; callers add no spacing. One file as its diff (with `lines`, folded in its own card past that many), several as a card of them ("3 files changed +18 −3", M/A/D, +n −n), a row opening its file and "View all" all of them, e.g. in the app's panel. AgentTurnSources: the pages the answer drew on as a row of chips, each a link with its icon and site. In an AgentTurnChangesProvider around the turn and its footer, AgentTurnChangesTrigger, the first child of the footer's AgentTurnInfo (one of its facts, "3 files changed +6 −1", one file too, and a small chevron, in their size and grey, hovered in the text's colour; a disclosure, kept with the last fact where the footer is narrow, its words cut first, and shown where the actions show on hover only; 44px under a finger with the footer no taller) opens the card under the answer, no rule, rendered only while open; open/defaultOpen/onOpenChange on the provider.

items.name: long-text
items.title: Long Text
items.description: Text whose runs without a space (a long address, base64, a hash) are folded past 1,024 characters, so its layout stays bounded whatever the text: a browser lays such a run out as one word broken anywhere, in time that grows with its length (WebKit) or, kerned in the system font, with its square (Chromium: 256 KiB of one letter, 3s a layout). A folded run (LongRun) shows its first 512 characters, an ellipsis, a button for 16,384 more at a time ("Show 261,632 more characters") and one to copy it whole, and is not kerned; in a link, only its start. LongText folds a string's runs, for text shown as written (a sent message's, ComposerMessage); Markdown folds its own, not in code blocks. Words, however many, are as they were.

items.name: markdown
items.title: Markdown
items.description: An agent's Markdown, streamed or not: Streamdown's, at the rhythm of a conversation (16px text on 28px lines, as ChatGPT's and Claude's answers, about 85 characters to the conversation's column; blocks 12px apart; headings h1 22px, h2 18px, the rest the text's size in bold; list items close and hanging from their markers, headings a step above the text, tables with rules between rows only and numbers lined up, over each its size, a button copying it (an HTML table a spreadsheet or document pastes as one, and Markdown text) and one showing it full screen with its heading held at the top; in a message scroller (itself @container/message-scroller) a table wider than the text takes the room either side, centred, as wide as its columns need, at most the scroller less 56px each side (48 past a scrollbar) and 1152px; while it streams, whole rows only, each fading in (a row waits for its line's end, the heading row for its rule, so no pipes first and no columns shifting with each word), quotes a rule and muted text), its fenced code a CodeBlock with line numbers, its file name (```ts title="build.ts") or language and a copy button and, with onOpenCode, a button that opens it whole, folded in its own card past 12 lines (`codeLines`, CodeBlock's `lines`), only those highlighted and rendered while folded, so a fence of thousands of lines costs a short one's. Footnotes are its sources: each mark a numbered tile, the notes a list under a rule with the site each links to. Its props are Streamdown's; the app's components replace these, e.g. links that open beside the conversation. With Streamdown's Mermaid plugin (plugins={{ mermaid }}, from @streamdown/mermaid, the app's dependency), ```mermaid blocks are diagrams in the theme's greys, light or dark, their code a toggle away; while they stream or if they cannot be drawn, their code shows. With Streamdown's math plugin (plugins={{ math }}, from @streamdown/math, the app's dependency with katex and its CSS), $$…$$ (and, with singleDollarTextMath, $…$) formulas render with KaTeX in the text's colour; while they stream or if KaTeX cannot read them their TeX shows as code, copying one copies its TeX, and a block formula wider than the lane scrolls, focusable. The app's CSS adds Streamdown's classes: @source "../node_modules/streamdown/dist/*.js". New blocks fade in (opacity, 600ms) while it streams (isAnimating), never when a finished message opens or with reduced motion. headingOffset sets the headings' aria-level below the page's, their size kept. A fenced code block whose lines are too long for it (they scroll, or wrap) has a wrap toggle in its header (labels.wrap), off by default; codeWrap starts its lines wrapped. Long words, paths and URLs wrap instead of widening the lane, inline code keeps its frame on every line, a chip keeps the punctuation after it on its line, table cells are capped at 24rem, wrapping and top-aligned (a table still wider scrolls, focusable to scroll by keyboard), and a numbered list's gutter grows with its widest number. A fenced block's code says its language (data-language), so a quote of it keeps its fence's. Its blocks are a flex column 12px apart, not block flow, so WebKit's selection shows their text only, as a list's, not a solid fill over the margins and line ends. linkIcon gives a link the app's icon for its site (e.g. a favicon), centred on the line in any script, apart from the text before it and kept with the link's words; a bare address breaks anywhere. linkProtocols allows an app's own link protocols (e.g. ["vesper"] for vesper://…), for it to render through components.a; the sanitizer is recognised by its function, so an app's own rehype-sanitize schema keeps them and the math attributes. A list's dot is centred on its first line at any line height. A run of over 1,024 characters without a space (an address, base64, a hash) is folded (long-text), so a layout stays bounded whatever the answer.

items.name: aspect-ratio-icon
items.title: Aspect Ratio Icon
items.description: A shape's aspect ratio as an icon, such as beside "16:9" in a choice of an image's or video's size: a frame of that shape, its long side the icon's; a ratio it cannot read (e.g. "auto") is a dashed square. Sized and coloured as Hugeicons' icons are, in buttons, menus and toggles.

items.name: status-mark
items.title: Status Mark
items.description: A status as a small mark, such as a conversation's, a connection's or a task's: a dot in its tone's colour (neutral, info, success, warning, destructive), a warning a ring and a danger a diamond so they are told apart by shape too, or a spinner while it is busy, in the text's colour with 2px lines so it is seen at a glance (still where the reader asks for less motion); `grey` where the page has no colour (a sidebar), the same shapes in greys; named for screen readers, its label in a tooltip on hover and while the keyboard is on its row. A status to read on screen is a Badge.

items.name: conversation-details
items.title: Conversation Details
items.description: A conversation's details, e.g. where it runs, its branch and changes, its subagents: a card of sections (a small grey heading with a count after it and a menu at its end, hairlines between them) of 32px rows, each an icon with a grey status mark at its corner (a spinner while running), its value with an optional muted label before it ("Effort High"), plain rows for facts that are not controls, mono meta at its end ("+38 −12", "19s"), a chevron or an icon button of its own, as a button, link or menu trigger. Pinned at the top right of the conversation's area, over the margin beside its column, where there is room, and shown and hidden by a button in the header; else that button opens it as a popover under it. It scrolls inside, no taller than the area. The app gives every row and word. The pinned card 192px, 3 columns and a gutter.

items.name: selection-actions
items.title: Selection Actions
items.description: A small toolbar by text the reader selects in a region, e.g. an agent's answer: Quote (SelectionQuote) and the app's own actions (SelectionAction), each handed the selection as Markdown (selectionMarkdown: bold, inline code, links, lists, headings, quotes and fenced code with its language; buttons and hidden text left out) and its range, then the selection cleared. All of them share one set of document listeners, and a change of selection renders only the region it is in. It shows for a selection with text that starts and ends in the region and not in a field: when a mouse drag ends, a frame after a keyboard or script selection, on touch once the selection has held still; above the selection, below it on a touch screen where the OS has its own menu. It takes neither focus nor the selection, follows the selection as the page scrolls and hides while it is out of view. Tab moves into it, the arrows between its buttons, Escape hides it and returns focus. Past maxLength characters it says the selection is too long instead of offering its actions. The app decides what an action does; a quote goes in the composer as a quote chip.

items.name: agent-app
items.title: Agent App
items.description: An agent app's shell: an optional rail of the app's areas (chat, files, settings) at the window's edge, kept while the sidebar is closed, the app's mark at its top, or (railPlacement="sidebar") a bar at the sidebar's foot at every width, as on a phone, with no column; a sidebar (its name and a new conversation, a search row with its keys, then 32px rows of 14px, a project's count or `meta` and a conversation's time at their ends, a conversation's `icon` before its title and its `detail` a second line under it, a project's `hint` after its name, open by default or as the app keeps them, `shown` up to all; SidebarEdge its edge) of projects (the directories conversations start in), flat, each to its page with its count, then the app's conversations (`layout` list, the default), or each opening to its latest conversations, then the conversations in no project (`tree`), or, with `groups` (places projects live, e.g. machines) and its segmented tabs, a collapsible section per group with its projects and conversations, an unavailable one marked, a project showing its conversations' most pressing status in greys by shape (in a tree, while closed); the main area a card on the sidebar's colour, right after the rail while the sidebar is closed or folded; on a touch screen the rail is the desktop's (48px, 32px icons, 44px targets unseen) and the sidebar keeps its own new conversation and search, 28px wider for its rows; under a finger the sidebar's edge is a handle to see (a thin line, 4 by 32px, darker as it is held), dragged without the page scrolling, a tap leaving it open; a header of where the reader is ("agentui / Fix the slow deploy", 13px); the conversation's column of 12 columns of 48px, 752px with 16px each side (AgentAppColumn) and the composer's place under it (AgentAppDock, the messages fading above it), or a new conversation's page (AgentAppStart): its composer already in an AgentAppDock, where the conversation's will be, and the heading centred in the room over it, which shrinks and scrolls first in a short window; the row above the composer where a new conversation's project is picked, optionally in labelled groups (e.g. by the machine they are on), each with its own "No project" and "Add project…", the trigger then naming the group (with one group, no headings and the plain names), gone once it has started; a project's page of all its conversations, with room for the app's own sections; and a resizable panel of the app's beside the main area, the sidebar closing to the rail while it is open, in one card with it split by a line (a conversation's files, or a Browser, whose tabs are then its bar), which can expand over it, and as a sheet or a phone's drawer over the whole window; the app's areas at the sidebar's foot. On a touch screen too narrow for the sidebar beside the conversation's 600px (a tablet upright), a list and its page: the sidebar open at its narrowest between the rail and a conversation of minTouchMainWidth (432px, a large phone's, so from 704px); narrower (an unfolded phone), the sidebar folds to the rail and opens as a sheet over the conversation. On a foldable open as a book, the conversation on one screen and the panel on the other, or with no panel the sidebar pinned open as the first screen; half open as a laptop (tabletop), the composer's dock on the bottom screen. On a phone the header is the sidebar's button, the title and the app's actions at a finger's size, the sidebar is a sheet ending with the app's areas, and the panel a sheet from the bottom. The app gives the data, the addresses and the menus, and routes. With titlebar, a desktop window's bar across the top: back, forward and the sidebar's button past the window's own buttons, the header in it, the rail and a card of the sidebar and main area under it, 8px from the window's end and foot, its corners rounded, dragged by the bar; a panel beside the main area has its bar in the bar's row over it, as wide as it (useAgentAppPanelBar for a content's own, e.g. a Browser's barContainer), the panel's one button (AgentAppPanelTrigger, then the bar's AgentAppPanelClose) at the window's end open or closed; without Window Controls Overlay (a WKWebView's) the app's --agent-app-titlebar-inset and --agent-app-titlebar-height on the root, and agentAppTitlebarControls for a host that drags the window itself. AgentAppSidebarTitle: the sidebar's header as a button (renaming the workspace), its words where a title's are and as heavy, its hover's grey 8px out; a chevron with `chevron`. AgentAppPage `tabs`: above its title, under the way back, 16px over the title (line tabs on a rule), the first tab's word on the page's start line, the title's and the content's. A conversation's `meta` (its facts: where, its branch, its cost, when) stands in columns on a project's page, lined up across its rows (ItemGroup `columns`), its status and buttons after them, `metaAlign` each column's start (words, the default) or end (numbers); on a phone, a line under its title. The pages' and AgentAppConversationList's density="compact": 32px rows, as the sidebar's, without an outline, for a long list. A dialog opened from the panel, open as the window narrows past the panel's room, stays on top and in reach: the panel's sheet or drawer opens once it closes. AgentAppPage's footer stays at the page's foot as it scrolls, on its colour, in its column: e.g. unsaved changes, an Alert with its AlertActions.

items.name: browser
items.title: Browser
items.description: Pages in tabs, as a browser has, e.g. for the panel beside a conversation (its bar in barContainer where given: an AgentApp titlebar's row over the panel, each pane's bar over its pane; its first tab and its toolbar on one start line, its last button and the toolbar's on one end line, 12px in; there its tabs as a desktop browser's on the frame: the one shown a solid piece 32px high of the panel's colour (a step lighter in dark), the others bare with a thin line between two, a piece of their own under the pointer, each with its close; as wide as 15rem, narrower as more open); its toolbar of islands, back, forward and a web page's reload one, the page's tools another, its address a pill ringed thinly only where the keyboard brought the focus (not a click, nor a new tab's focus as it opens): web pages in a frame (its sandbox the app's) or the app's own; code (a CodeViewer), diffs, images, video, audio, PDFs, tables (a CSV), terminals and folders in their viewers. Each tab goes back and forward through what was opened in it, or is one of the app's fixed areas (pinned: no close button); a diff of more than one file lists them over the one picked, with the app's actions (Discard, Commit) in a bar at its foot; on coarse pointers the diff shows its file icon, name and translatable Unified label even with the file list, with signs alone and no numbers or hunk headers; touch tabs have equal segments, across the bar on phones and content-wide from 640px; its toolbar (or its viewer's) says where the page is, and a web page's address can be changed: every address, typed or a recent one, goes through resolveAddress (by default resolveWebAddress, http for a local host and its port, https for the rest), and the empty bar says what it takes. A web page (a frame, the app's screenshot of it, or a remote browser's live page: its frames pictures drawn once decoded, a canvas the app draws into or a video it plays, the reader's pointer, wheel, keys, an input method's composition and paste sent back in the page's CSS pixels, its cursor, and its select popups and script dialogs drawn by agentui; by touch, the screen's keyboard only while the page has a caret) shows in the panel's size or a device's, with whether its server runs (or a page saying nothing does, or that it did not load, with Retry), the agent at work in it (what it does, its pointer, the reader taking over), the reader pointing at an element of it for the chat, a dark color scheme kept by tab, and its console and requests in a fixed 250px drawer with an always-visible tool (disabled without data): agentui draws the chrome, the app gives the states. The app opens pages (a new tab, or in the tab shown) and changes them as they load or grow; the state is the browser's own or the app's. A page in a viewer is named by its tab, not again in the viewer's toolbar (back and forward alone at its start; a folder keeps its path, the way up), where it is on the tab's hover.

items.name: clamp
items.title: Clamp
items.description: Content cut to a number of lines (6 by default), fading out, with a row under it: a button that shows it all, how many lines and words it has (each Chinese or Japanese character a word) and the app's actions (copy, open in a reader); in the color of the text around it, so it suits any bubble. Open and scrolled past its start, a bar sticks to the top saying whose it is and how far the reader is, and closes it, its start brought back into view. Focus moving into the cut-off part shows it. A bubbling revealmatch event with detail.range opens it when the match reaches below the cut.

items.name: user-message
items.title: User Message
items.description: A message the user sent, at the end of the line: where it came from over it ("Sent from queue"), its text in a muted bubble cut to 6 lines with a Clamp (how long it is, copy, open in a reader; a bar at the top while it is open and scrolled past), when it was sent and its actions under it, shown on hover or focus and always on touch screens. Files, images and links it refers to are MessageMention chips in its text, each a button opening what it refers to. A command in its text ("/review") is a MessageCommand, a chip in monospace; a message that is only a command ("/compact") is a UserMessageCommand in place of the bubble, a quiet monospace line on a hairline at its end, what it did following as the app's own (a MessageDivider). Each message has an sr-only author heading, its level a prop (h3 by default). With from, a message written by someone else folds to one line showing the app-provided icon, label and first non-empty summary line. MessageLink: a web address in its text as a link, the site's icon (`icon`) before it centred on the line in any script and apart from the text before it, a long address going on beside it and breaking anywhere. At most 9 of the conversation's 12 columns (docs/grid.md).

items.name: message-scroller-load-earlier
items.title: Message Scroller Load Earlier
items.description: Loads the messages before those a long conversation shows: a button floating at the top of a MessageScroller, shown while the reader is at the start or while they load, with a spinner and no second load while they do; hidden once they came in above, it hands the focus to the viewport.

items.name: message-outline
items.title: Message Outline
items.description: A long message with its outline: once it is 3 views tall and has two headings or more, its headings beside it where there is room, sticking to the top (the section being read marked, those read darker, how far the reader is, previous and next section, open in a reader), and otherwise a button sticking to the top that says the section being read and opens the outline, or nothing with pill false (e.g. beside a ConversationMinimap, which has its sections); while more than a view is below, a button at the bottom jumps to its end. A heading chosen scrolls into view and takes focus.

items.name: conversation-minimap
items.title: Conversation Minimap
items.description: A conversation map with one tick per user message and the app's marks, its reply's sections (the app's `sections`, or its headings read from the reply while rendered) as ticks under it; the ticks fall off as a dock's icons, the one being read longest (24px) and darkest, each row further a step shorter and lighter, short and faint (8px) from the fifth on, centred on the row under the pointer or with focus while one is, a section or mark a step behind a turn; hovered or focused, a tick's card: the question's first line, the reply's opening (the app's `reply`, or its first paragraph) in two lines, its attachments and its sections, the hovered one bold. Click or Enter jumps there; arrows move between ticks, with previous and next turn buttons. The error kind is a graphite diamond; a mark is a shorter tick. Shows only where the margin beside an AgentAppColumn has room, below a pinned ConversationDetails card, hiding when too little height is left. Hidden on touch screens and phones and when the conversation fits. Use inside MessageScrollerProvider beside the viewport.

items.name: message-reader
items.title: Message Reader
items.description: A message to read on its own, over the conversation: its title and what it is, a search of its text alone (Ctrl or Cmd F, Enter and Shift+Enter through the matches, drawn as CSS highlights), the app's actions and ⋯ menu, its outline beside it where the dialog (not the window) is wide enough and how far the reader is along the top, its text at a reading size. On a phone it is the whole screen, with back, the title, the menu, and a bar of the outline, search, how far and the actions. It opens as DialogContent's size="full".

items.name: conversation-find
items.title: Conversation Find
items.description: Ctrl/⌘F searches a whole mounted conversation’s DOM text, including folded parts and content-visibility-skipped messages. Reveals hidden=until-found folds with beforematch (closed folds hold only their text, FoldFindText, not their content) and clipped parts with revealmatch, draws up to 1000 matches in greys ("1 of 1000+"), and returns focus on close. Its words are labels. In a windowed MessageScroller it has every message mounted while open (useMessageScrollerShowAll); messages the app has not rendered and deferred steps not loaded yet are outside the search. Without CSS highlights, count, navigation, reveal and scroll still work.

items.name: todo-list
items.title: Todo List
items.description: A list of things to do, such as an agent's plan, flat in the conversation: its title and how many are done (a bar and "2 of 5"), then the items, the one in progress in bold with a spinner, those done muted and struck through; each item's status is read out. In a PopoverContent it has no border of its own: the popover's surface its edge, out to its edges past the popover's padding.

items.name: plan-card
items.title: Plan Card
items.description: An agent's proposed plan, flat in the conversation with a hairline border: its title, copy and the app's actions above Markdown folded to a number of lines, Revise and Implement across its foot. Once decided, AgentRequest's quiet row records the outcome and opens the original plan without its choices; focus follows the decision to the row.

items.name: conversation-skeleton
items.title: Conversation Skeleton
items.description: A conversation not here yet (ConversationSkeleton): a message asked, at the end edge in a bubble the user's message's size and corners, and the lines of an answer in the conversation's type (16px on lines of 28px); a status named by label ("Loading conversation"), seen only past a short wait (animate-wait-in) so a quick load never flashes it. SkeletonLines: lines of text not here yet, each a thin rounded bar on a line of the text's height, so the place is as tall as the text will be; widths one a line.

items.name: message-divider
items.title: Message Divider
items.description: An event in a conversation, between its messages (a day, the context compacted, the model switched, a branch): one centred line of small muted text between rules, an icon first, what can be followed a button a little brighter. With running, its words shimmer, respecting reduced motion; a compaction marker can show context compacted, compacting or failed with an icon and words.

items.name: message-error
items.title: Message Error
items.description: Why a turn failed and what comes next, where its answer would have gone: an outlined card in the page's greys, an alert's triangle, the reason in a line and, under it, what it means or, while the app waits to try again, a countdown to it and which attempt that is; "Retry now" or the app's own action ("Continue") at its end. Its status, told by its mark and words, not a colour: waiting (a clock, the countdown), retrying (a spinner), exhausted ("Gave up after 5 attempts"), failed, cancelled, unknown (no answer: it may have gone through, check before trying again); several actions of the app's wrap at its end; nothing is tried on its own, the countdown's end only says it retries.

items.name: composer
items.title: Composer
items.description: A chat's message box: text with chips in it for mentions, files (an image's thumbnail, an upload's progress or why it failed) and links, at the caret where they came in, or files in a row above it: images as 64px tiles in a sideways-scrolling line (a progress ring or warning over the image, remove/retry on the corner on hover or focus, always on touch or error), other files as 44px cards (a 32px icon or upload ring, the name over its state, a round × always on the corner, a failed one's edge dashed), or as the text's chips; a pasted address becomes a titled link once the app resolves it, with a bar to keep it as a link, a preview or plain text; a chip is selected by Backspace or the arrows and shows a card to open, retry or remove it; mentions suggested as you type a trigger such as @ or #, the list under the trigger, the send button grey while it is open (Enter takes a suggestion); Enter sends and Shift+Enter adds a line (not while an input method composes, nor on touch screens); inside a ``` code block Enter adds a line keeping the indent and never sends, Enter at the closing fence or after two blank lines leaves the block, Tab and Shift+Tab indent and outdent the lines, pastes stay typed text and mentions are not suggested; one button sends or stops the running response without losing focus, and while a turn runs says what sending does (followUp: send, queue or steer) by its icon and name, with a tooltip naming the Cmd/Ctrl-click alternative; past eight lines it scrolls and expands (Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E) to a page of writing with a word count, its Markdown styled as typed (marks kept and muted, headings semibold, code in mono; the text unchanged), and a Markdown preview (ComposerEditor's previewProps: Markdown's labels, headingOffset and other props); files come in by an attach button, pasting or dropping, and long pasted text can come in as a file. Its box has the theme's rounded-composer corner and a shadow for its edge (no border, so no focus outline: the caret shows focus; a border in forced colors); the toolbar's menus open 8px above it, not over the text (popups="trigger": by their buttons instead). Where its toolbar is narrower than 36rem (a phone, or beside a sidebar on an unfolded foldable), or where unfolded its tools do not fit (a picker's value cut short), a step at a time (a compact ComposerOptionsFold to its icon and the rest, its value gone, in place first; those not keep away next), ComposerOptions folds the tools in ComposerOptionsFold (permissions, the context meter) behind one button and a sheet of ComposerOptionsItem rows; a folded picker opened from a row opens from that button. ComposerTakeover puts what the agent waits for (an agent-request: an approval, a question) in the composer's place and frame, one at a time, under a line of the app's status and a stop, a question settable aside to chat; the composer stays mounted, hidden and inert, its draft kept, and focus moves to the request and back to the editor. A request arriving while the reader types is held until they pause (holdWhileTyping, 1.5s by default), or at once on blur or send; the composer keeps focus and keystrokes, with a quiet hint announced politely. ComposerMessage shows a sent message's chips the same way. ComposerShelf sits over the composer tucked under its top edge, a little narrower; several stack edge to edge, square where they meet with one hairline, fading in; ComposerShelfTab is a small content-width tab at the top-right edge whose count lifts once when it rises (not with reduced motion); the app renders shelves in a fixed order so rows never swap. ComposerVoice dictates: tapped it records until Done, held (pointer or Space) until let go, slid back to cancel; the time and a waveform in the text's place, or a live transcript (transcript, its interim words grey) as the text will be, the time on the toolbar; why it would not start under the box, by getUserMedia's error names (access off, no microphone); a take whose words could not be made out kept, with Retry; maxDuration counting its last 10 seconds down; submitOnFinish sending at once (always, or when held). A shortcut (a KeyboardEvent.code, e.g. AltRight) drives it from anywhere in the window, pressed alone: held, it records until let go (Escape cancels); tapped, until tapped again; another key with it (an Option or AltGr character) starts none or cancels it and goes through; the window left while held finishes it, unsent; of several composers, the one with the focus answers, else the one that last had it; labels.shortcut in the mic's tooltip, aria-keyshortcuts. While onStart is pending, a spinner in the mic's glyph's place (still with reduced motion), the mic busy and described as starting; ready (the app keeps the microphone open, a press records at once) shows on the idle mic as its glyph in the text's colour and a dot at its corner, described as Microphone ready. holdToTalk, on a touch screen: a tap on the composer types, a long press (400ms, before the platform's) talks: with the keyboard down anywhere on the composer, the editor too (its selection and callout held off for that press), with the editor focused only off its text; held, its words, time and waveform over the conversation, what letting go does, and Cancel and To text targets for the finger (lit, saying what letting go there does, a short vibration); let go elsewhere, its words are sent alone, the draft kept (onSubmit's options.talk), on To text they go in at the caret, the editor focused; a finger moved first is a scroll, a second finger or a cancelled touch drops it, the page hidden puts it in the text. However a take ends, the editor has the focus again, the caret after its words or where it was (the focus fell to the page, where typing went nowhere; in WebKit the caret went to the start). Given inputs, a chevron beside the mic (a split button; tap, hold and Space stay the mic's) opens a choice of what to record from, the system default first, a sheet on a phone, not while recording or starting; the app lists the devices (onInputsOpen to list them again), keeps the choice (input, onInputChange) and records from it. Built on Lexical, which apps do not see. A quote (e.g. from selection-actions) is a chip of its first words, its card its source and whole text with Open (onOpenQuote, also Enter) and Remove; copied as a Markdown quote.

items.name: composer-queue
items.title: Composer Queue
items.description: The messages queued while a turn runs, on a shelf above a composer: each can be edited (not one marked `editable: false`, e.g. a queued command, with its `icon` before its text), one from elsewhere says where (`from`: another agent or session, by weight before its text, cut to a third of the row, read with it and able to hold a link; over its text in the manager), moved to the top, sent now or removed, and moved by dragging or with Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown, which screen readers hear; past three it shows the first and how many more, and opens a dialog to filter, select, edit, move and remove them all. Shows a message being sent and a paused queue (resume, clear). On a phone, one row over the composer that opens the dialog full screen. The app owns the queue; the shelf asks for changes.

items.name: composer-select
items.title: Composer Select
items.description: A choice of one from a composer's toolbar, such as a mode or an agent: a trigger that says the choice, and its items (a label, a line of description, a detail, a tick on the chosen one) over the composer, a search over more than searchFrom of them (10; 0 for always) that filters them by their words and keywords, in their order, its match in the text's colour, the chosen one still chosen while filtered out, a pinned item never filtered out nor marked, the search's text the app's with search and onSearchChange, and says when nothing matches, or in a sheet from the bottom with a title and Done on a phone (below sm, 640px: useComposerPhone). Arrow keys move among the items, Enter, Space or a click chooses and closes. ComposerModePicker: the app's modes; one with tone "destructive" (it lets the agent act unasked) is, chosen, in the destructive colour in the toolbar, its icon too, and its icon so in the list; a footer under the modes is a line of small grey text with a link or button in it (ComposerSelectContent's footer, past a hairline, in sight while the list scrolls). Its row look (composerSelectRow) and parts are what model-picker is built on. ComposerOptionButton: a button in the trigger's look, out of a ComposerSelect, for an option of the composer's row that opens something else (a dialog) or acts at once, a chevron after its words with `chevron`.

items.name: model-picker
items.title: Model Picker
items.description: Picks a conversation's model and how hard it thinks, from a trigger in a composer's toolbar (a sheet from the bottom on a phone): the trigger says the model, its route's tag and its thinking step ("Opus 5.5 · High", "deepseek-v4 OpenRouter"), or asks to pick a model when there is none or it cannot be used. With several groups, a rail of them (each its icon and name, Recent first; a tablist) beside the list shows one group's models at a time, cut short at groupLimit with how many more; the chosen model's group is the one open; on a phone the rail is a row of tabs above the list. ← from an empty search goes to the rail, ↑↓ there change group, → or typing goes back to the search (mirrored right to left). A single group's models are listed directly under its name, recent models only while groupLimit cuts it short. Typing searches them all, under their groups' names, "3 of 49" at the search's end. The thinking steps are one row, its name, a slider of named steps, the chosen step's name and, off the model's default, a button back to it (EffortSlider: a dot for each, a grey fill, a note or a warning under it); a model's row is its name and tick, its detail on the highlighted row; with few models (searchFrom, 10) one list under the groups' names, no search or rail; Manage models the last row, the shortcut in the trigger's tooltip; every row 32px, the list and rail as tall as the taller of the rail and the shown group's list, the popover's bottom kept as the group changes that follows the model, a switch for a model that only turns thinking on or off, ←→ from the list with one group; a step the model lacks runs at its default and says so. A last row turns the popover to the models for images, video and speech, each a page with its settings for the conversation as rows. A purpose with no models says so (labels.purposeEmpty) over the app's next step (its empty). Every row is a row's height, Manage models too; a model's name is never cut for its details, which take the rest of the row and are cut first. Extra content (children) shows only when there is some: a set of conditions all false leaves no empty band. A group is the app's: a provider or a family. Models, groups, steps and purposes are the app's data. With showGroupIcon, the trigger shows the chosen model's group's icon before its name. A group's own header (groups[].header) over its models while they are shown: its tab's pane, or under its heading in a list of all; not in a search's results. A section's heading in the rail may have a mark (its first group's sectionIcon). A model's section (a family) lists a group's models in runs under a heading each, after those with none; a search by group alone. customInput (with onCustomModel) keeps a field at the list's bottom, sticky in the pane, for a model id not listed, Enter giving it to onCustomModel, which is told where the id was typed (onCustomModel(id, { group, page }): the pane's group, none in a search across groups; the page, none for the main one). pages are rows under the list opening pages of further groups (rail, search) under a back header, Back or Escape returning; their models picked as any; onPageChange(id | null) says one opened or was left (e.g. to fetch its groups), and a page's loading shows the spinner row in place of empty panes. A model's disabledReason says why it cannot be used, at its row's end and in its name. A chosen model gone from the list or not usable (valueLabel for its name) stays chosen, the trigger its name with a warning ("Opus 4, not available") and a line over the list saying so; nothing replaces it. source says where the chosen model comes from under the list, with Pin or Unpin (pinned, onPinnedChange; a promise shows saving, a rejection that it failed). No models at all is "No models yet", a search's none "No models found"; error with onRetry, a row saying why, with Retry.

items.name: chip
items.title: Chip
items.description: A chip's look, once for every chip: a file, an image, a link, a quote or a mention in a line of text, 24px tall, its icon or thumbnail first, then its name and a grey detail, on a hairline; muted on a field (the composer's; in dark, the page's colour, recessed in it), raised on a tint (a sent message's bubble), outline on the page (12px, grey, e.g. an answer's sources) and 26px (md) in a row of its own. Chip is a span of it, chipVariants the classes for a button or link, ChipList a wrapping row of them.

items.name: auth-page
items.title: Auth Page
items.description: A sign-in or sign-up page, the app's form in it. Wide (48rem and up, by its own width): two halves, the app's aside on the muted grey at the start (the brand at the top, its title, h2, and words at the foot) and the form on the page's colour at the end, its title (h1, text-display) and description over it, switchTo (e.g. a link to sign up) at the top's end on the brand's line, terms at the foot. Narrow: the form on a card on the grey, the brand and switchTo above it, the terms under it; the aside only with asideOnNarrow. The app puts in its form and its words, no styles of its own. With titlebar, in a desktop window whose own buttons are over the page, a bar across its top as high as the window's title bar (env(titlebar-area-height), else --agent-app-titlebar-height on the root, else 40px) drags the window as an AgentApp titlebar does, the page 8px under it. Wide or narrow by its own width, measured (data-wide, group-data-wide/auth: for the app's), not a container query, so no size container wraps the form's own.

items.name: floating-button
items.title: Floating Button
items.description: A button that floats over what it covers, e.g. one that jumps to the end of a long text or of a terminal's output: round, on the page's colour (a step lighter in dark) and raised by shadow-float, as the message scroller's button is.

items.name: picture-in-picture
items.title: Picture in Picture
items.description: A small window in a corner of its place (the nearest positioned ancestor, e.g. the main area) showing what an agent is on while the conversation goes on: of its items (pages, terminals), the one it is on (active), following it from one to the next. Dots (or "2/12" past seven; under a finger 28px wide each, so a tap takes its own, a count past four and in a pill) say how many there are; a swipe across the preview (taken on past its side, a move: the window catches up with the finger), a sideways scroll, the left and right arrows or a dot go through them, and it then stays where the reader went, a Follow button taking it back (following, onFollowingChange; onShownChange says which it shows, e.g. to stream that one's frames only). Each is a card (its title and preview, at aspectRatio 16:10; 320px wide, 240px on a phone) or a pill of one line (its icon, line and status; up to 384px, 240px on a phone), as its form says or the reader makes it (Minimize; the pill's line shows the card again, or expands one with no preview); a terminal is best a pill of its last line, PictureInPictureLines its last lines for a card. Dragged by any part but its buttons, it lands in the corner it is let go nearest or thrown towards, sliding there (none with reduced motion), or, let go with its middle past a side or thrown out past the side it is at, tucks into it, a 24px tab left; a tap on its preview is still a press; Shift and the arrow keys move it. corner/defaultCorner/onCornerChange in the reading direction, 16px (inset) from its place's edges and the safe areas. An item's attention is a strip under a card or the pill's line, in the text's colour with a ring, read out, the window nudged once. Expand (onExpand(id), e.g. into the side panel) and Close (onClose) are the app's; the app renders it while it shows.

items.name: code-readout
items.title: Code Readout
items.description: A short code read out to be typed elsewhere (a sign-in's one-time code, a device's pairing code): 32px on 40px lines (the theme's text-readout), monospaced, its characters in groups (`group`, 4 by default) apart by a margin, not spaces, so it is copied and selected whole; read out character by character to a screen reader, its `label` first. Beside it, a CopyButton with `showLabel`.

items.name: stat
items.title: Stat
items.description: Headline numbers and facts of a page: StatGrid (as many columns as fit, each at least 192px, 16px apart), Stat (a card's hairline edge, 16px in) of StatLabel (13px, grey), StatValue (22px, text-display, tabular) and StatDetail (a line in the faintest grey); and FactList, a row of Facts under a page's title, each its label small and grey over its value, 24px apart, wrapping where narrow (a description list).

items.name: copy-button
items.title: Copy Button
items.description: An icon button that copies a value, such as a reply, or an image (CopyData: a type and its blob, asked for on the press; several in an array are one copy, e.g. a table as text/html and text/plain): its name and tooltip say "Copied" for a while after (pressed, the tooltip stays open to say so), and screen readers hear it. A value that has changed since (e.g. streaming) is not claimed as copied; when the clipboard refuses, it says it could not copy. With `showLabel`, its word beside the icon ("Copy", then "Copied"), as wide as the wider of them so it does not jump, and no tooltip.

items.name: qr-code
items.title: QR Code
items.description: A string as an SVG QR code, e.g. a link for a phone to scan: one path for all modules, crisp edges, a quiet zone of 4 modules, an error-correction level (M by default), a name for screen readers (never the value), and a caption under it. The plate stays white in the dark theme, as scanners need dark modules on a light plate. Made with uqr.

items.name: table-preview
items.title: Table Preview
items.description: A table of the app's to look at, copy and download, framed as a code block: its title and size, a button to copy it as text a spreadsheet takes, a menu to download it as CSV or Markdown, and a full-screen view with its heading row kept at the top. It scrolls sideways where it is wider, by keyboard too, faded at the edges; long cells wrap, short ones stay one line, a column of numbers to the end; a cell's rendering (e.g. a search's matches) and where a download goes may be the app's. Made of shadcn's Table, Dialog and DropdownMenu, in the code block's frame. It opens as DialogContent's size="full".

items.name: search-highlight
items.title: Search Highlight
items.description: Where a search's terms are in a text, as the reader would find them (any case, full-width or not, a letter and its accents one), at the text's own places; marked in text or in a node of text, e.g. a line of coloured code, a match across its elements marked in each. Each match a soft tint (a match across elements one band), the current one filled, in the theme's colours; in a tooltip, inverted as its surface is.

items.name: usage-meter
items.title: Usage Meter
items.description: How much of something is used, as a meter (role=meter, its name and value said): a ring or a bar in the foreground's greys, the app's words after it, on its own or in a Badge as a quota chip. Its breakdown's popover is no wider or higher than the room it has, its rows scrolling (a keyboard stop where they do), its title, meter and footer kept; contentClassName gives it the app's classes. UsageMeterBreakdown is a button with the meter that opens a popover: its title and value on one line, a bar of the whole, and the app's rows of label and value in grey; rows with an amount are parts of the bar, each a grey of its own (no colour), and a row's separator starts a group (e.g. cost after context). In an input group, as a composer's toolbar, it opens 8px above the group, not over its text. Every word is the app's. Its fill in the theme's warning or destructive colour with `tone`, near a limit and at it, on the ring, the bar and the breakdown's bar, the track as it was. UsageMeterList: several meters at a glance (a popup of an account's limits), each its label and value on a line, a bar across under them and a line of detail (when it resets), 12px apart, each a meter to a screen reader.

items.name: usage-summary
items.title: Usage Summary
items.description: What a run used and what it cost, by unit, never added across units: a button of its totals (UsageAmount: the app's formatted value, its unit, its completeness), each saying how far it is to be trusted in words, not a colour (≈ and Estimated, Partial, Not reconciled, No price; not known is "Unknown", never 0); "So far" while it runs; opened, its breakdown (UsageSummaryRows: a row's label, amount and completeness, a button to its source and why, a popover, by touch too) and what has no price (missing). UsageSummaryRows alone goes in an AgentTurnInfo's details. The app adds the amounts, by unit; it fetches nothing.

items.name: connection
items.title: Connection
items.description: Connections to services (a model provider's, a tool server's), read, never managed. ConnectionList of ConnectionListItem: a row a connection, its name cut to a line and its status under it, a button that shows it (aria-current while shown); loading, its rows' shapes; none, labels.empty or the app's empty (a filter's "No match"); not fetched (error), why and Retry. Filtering and pages are the app's around it. ConnectionStatus: available, rejected, unknown or off, told by its mark's shape (a dot, a diamond, a ring, a bar) and its word, when it was checked and, too old to go by, "May be out of date"; why under it. ConnectionDetails (none chosen, loading, unavailable, or its parts): ConnectionDetailsHeader (its name whole and its status), ConnectionNotice (what needs the reader, e.g. to enter its key again, and the app's link to how), ConnectionDetailsField, ConnectionTarget (an address in mono on a line, a button showing it whole where it is cut short, one copying it) and ConnectionCredential (the app's masked summary, with a lock: no way to show or enter it).

items.name: diff-block
items.title: Diff Block
items.description: A unified diff, as git or diff -u writes it, in code blocks: one for each file, its icon, name (both, renamed or copied) and what it adds and removes (+3 −1, small, in the faintest grey) in the header, each line with its number in a gutter (a removed line's in the old file; or old and new, `numbers="both"`) and its sign in a column of its own, hunks under their @@ line as a band between rules where a file has more than one; added and removed lines in the code block's greys; a binary file says so. parseUnifiedDiff reads the text into files, hunks and lines (their numbers, renames, copies, modes, binary files and the no-newline marker); the block takes the text or what it read. With `lines`, each file longer than that folds in its own block (CodeBlock's `lines`, its words in `labels`), only the lines it shows rendered while folded. DiffFileContent is a file's lines alone, e.g. in a viewer; its touch option hides numbers and hunk headers on coarse pointers, leaving signs alone. labels.unified names the unified view. DiffFileList lists the files a diff changes (an M, A or D, the path with its directory fainter, +n −n) to pick one, as a panel's list or in DiffFilesCard, a message's card of a turn's changes ("3 files changed +18 −3" and the app's action, e.g. Review all).

items.name: code-viewer
items.title: Code Viewer
items.description: A file's code to read, from the code block: coloured, its lines numbered, folding by indentation in any language, wrapped or not (the app's to keep), JSON formatted or as written, its lines' look the app's (e.g. an edit's changes), and a find bar of its own: Ctrl+F or Cmd+F while the focus is in it, Enter and Shift+Enter to the next and previous match, :120 to line 120, its matches marked in the coloured code: CSS highlights of the lines in sight, so a keystroke renders no line again (5 ms, not 70, for a term in every line of 3,500), marks where the browser has none. Embedded (variant="embedded"), it is a viewer's, as the browser's code pages: in a ViewerFrame of its own, borderless to its edges as a diff is, its tools (format, find, copy) in the frame's toolbar, Wrap, its language and length in the status bar.

items.name: tool-call-data
items.title: Tool Call Data
items.description: A tool call's input or output, to read, for a call the app has no view of its own for (e.g. an MCP tool's): a JSON object, as text or a value, as its fields, each its key beside its value (over it where narrow): text as text, wrapped, its lines kept, long text cut to 6 lines over "Show all"; a number, true, false or null as code; an object, an array or text that is one in JSON as a formatted JSON block folding past 8 lines. Other text is text, coloured in its language ("ansi" for a terminal's), folding past 12 lines. Its header has its title, the app's actions, a toggle to the JSON as it came (formatted, wrapped) and copy, which copies it as it came. mcpToolName reads an MCP tool's name (mcp__github__create_issue) as its server and tool, for the app's title.

items.name: media-gallery
items.title: Media Gallery
items.description: Media in a message, in their order: images, videos and recordings. An image on its own is in a card as a video is, at its own shape (no taller than 240px, its size read as it loads where the app does not know it), its title, caption (a description, an end such as its cost) and actions under it: the app's, then copying it (as PNG) and opening it in a new tab, which every image has; more are square thumbnails, the last saying how many more, or each in its card (layout flow). Each opens a viewer of them all, copied and opened from there too, gone through with the arrow keys or its buttons, that returns focus to where it was opened (or the app's onOpen). One being made (pending, of the size or shape asked for) is a placeholder of its shape, its words shimmering with how long it has taken; one deferred loads when the reader asks (its size on the button, the app's onLoadRequest); one that could not be made or cannot load says so; the rest load as they near the viewport, an image's thumbnail over its placeholder (e.g. a ThumbHash's) standing in at its shape till it is drawn, and of its srcSet copies the one sharp enough for the width it is shown at. Videos and recordings have the same states, a video's placeholder at the shape asked for, a recording's where its controls go. A video or a recording is a card with Media Viewer's controls (over a video, under a recording), its title, the app's description, its length, actions and a transcript to open; a video at its own shape no taller than 400px, its place kept before it loads. One plays at a time in a gallery, or across a conversation in a MediaGalleryProvider; mediaProps give the app the element. On the conversation's 12 columns: an image alone at most 6, of two 6 each, of more 4, a thumbnail 3 (docs/grid.md). Its viewer's copy and open buttons are 32px beside the dialog's close, on its line.

items.name: agent-launch
items.title: Agent Launch
items.description: New tasks an agent proposes to start (each a conversation of its own), in an agent-request that asks the reader first, read at a glance rather than as a form: each AgentLaunch three lines in line with each other, its title (AgentLaunchTitle, one line), what it runs with as one quiet line cut short, its values a dot apart (AgentLaunchMeta of AgentLaunchMetaItem: the agent and model, the machine, the folder, the permissions; the dots not read out), and two lines of the first message it is sent (AgentLaunchMessage). A pencil at the title's end opens its settings in place, Done closes them: the title its editor (an Input), then a composer's box (AgentLaunchEdit: an InputGroup of the message, three lines to eight, and along its foot AgentLaunchControls, the pickers quiet as a composer's toolbar has them: ComposerSelect, a model picker, ComposerModePicker, an option a ComposerOptionButton with aria-pressed). What cannot change (a copy's agent, machine, folder: AgentLaunchMetaItem fixed, put first) stays a line over the box. Several are an AgentLaunchList, a rule between, each with a checkbox to leave it out (included, onIncludedChange; named by its title), its title and message muted when left out. The request's choices (Don't start, Always start like this, Start) are the app's, in AgentRequestFooter. Fits the composer's width on a phone (ComposerTakeover).

items.name: voice-mode
items.title: Voice Mode
items.description: A spoken conversation with the agent, the audio the app's: an orb (VoiceModeOrb) whose rings swell with the level of whoever is heard (the reader listening, the agent speaking; a CSS variable, set as often as the app likes), its disc breathing while it thinks, faint while it connects, grey with the mic struck out while muted, still where less motion is asked for, a button that interrupts the agent while it speaks (onInterrupt); a word of where it is, announced (VoiceModeStatus); the last lines said (VoiceModeCaptions of VoiceModeCaption, the agent's in the text's colour, the reader's grey, interim greyer), not announced; round buttons (VoiceModeControls: VoiceModeMute, pressed while muted, VoiceModeEnd, and the app's VoiceModeButton). variant full fills its place (a panel, a sheet, a phone's page): the orb 192px (160 on a phone) and its status in the middle, three lines of captions fading upward, the buttons at the foot over the home indicator. variant bar is a 56px row in the composer's place, as its box: a small orb, the status (read out only on a phone), the latest line kept to its end as it grows, the buttons.

items.name: agent-request
items.title: Agent Request
items.description: The agent asks the reader: to allow a tool call, or a question.
