A card for the composer's place (ComposerTakeover) in its frame, taking focus there, its icon beside its title and description (which name and describe it), what it is about under them (a command, a Questionnaire's choices, each led by its number, a checkbox after it where several may be chosen) and the reader's choices across its foot after a muted status ("Asked 4s ago"). Given its decision, it is one quiet row, as a step: the icon, what was asked and what came of it ("Allowed git push origin main", the question and its answer), its meta at the end ("Once · by you"); opened, the card as it was, to read, without its choices, a question's options listed with the chosen one marked. Given waiting, a still row for the conversation while the card is below ("Waiting for you below"). Several questions are one card, one at a time: a QuestionnaireProgress first in its footer and a QuestionnaireNavigation last, so there is always a way on; decided, each an AgentRequestQuestion over its options. While it asks, a chevron at its top end folds it to its title or header (collapsed, defaultCollapsed, onCollapsedChange; its words in labels), so the conversation over it can be read; its title opens it again, what was chosen in it kept. collapsible={false}: no chevron, a notice of one action in the composer's place (a sign-in, a limit reached). Of its title and a choice or two alone ("Working in another app", Take over), one row of 44px, the choices at its end on the card, no band under it and no chevron, at any width. AgentRequestError: why the reader's choice did not go through, over the footer, announced, in the destructive colour. Narrow, the AgentRequestStatus is a line of its own under the choices.

items.name: input-group
items.title: Input Group
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova input-group, fixed: the group looks disabled only when its input or textarea is, not when a button in an addon is; a contenteditable control, :focus-visible whenever it has focus, darkens the border a step instead of the dark border and 3px ring; a popup opened from inside the group, as a menu of a composer's toolbar, sits 8px clear of the whole group rather than of its trigger (inputGroupPopupOffset, Base UI's sideOffset for it), so it never covers the text; where the group folds its trigger away, it opens from the group's button marked data-input-group-fold (inputGroupPopupAnchor, Base UI's anchor for it). InputGroup size="lg": a sign-in screen's, 44px, its text 16px and its icons 20px. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: marker
items.title: Marker
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova marker, fixed: a marker that is a button or link takes a rounded focus ring, as the trace's, not the browser's square outline; the separator is a step smaller (12px text in a 24px row), as a divider in a conversation. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: message-scroller
items.title: Message Scroller
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova message-scroller, on @shadcn/react 0.3.1's primitive made part of it (message-scroller-primitive) and fixed: scrolling costs a few rect reads a frame however long the conversation, not every message's on every scroll event (each a forced layout of the whole conversation where layout was dirty); its messages windowed (windowed, on by default): each item keeps its place and height but the content of those more than a few views away is unmounted (10rem before first measured), mounted again as the reader comes near, before the frame is drawn where a scroll outruns the observers (a fling, a scrollbar drag, a jump, a conversation opened at a message: they were drawn as empty boxes until a later frame), except one holding the focus or a selection; useMessageScrollerShowAll(active) mounts them all, as a find does while open; windowed={false} keeps all mounted with content-visibility: auto; while the reader scrolls, what they look at stays put as messages above it mount or render at their real height (every row, with a messageId or not), in every browser (WebKit has no scroll anchoring and Firefox's missed these, so the browser's is off on the viewport); only a gesture toward the start (a wheel up, a finger dragging down, ArrowUp, PageUp, Home, Shift+Space) lets autoScroll go, as one toward the end at the end moves nothing and nothing would take it back up; nor does a message rebuilt in place, its nodes taken out and put back with a layout read between (as a renderer finishing a streamed reply does): the browser moved the scroll up as if the message were gone, which read as the reader scrolling away, and the reply was no longer followed (in WebKit, at every reply's end); the scroll-to-start button jumps, so with autoScroll it is not pulled back to the end, and scrollToMessage keeps the message in place while the messages above it render at their real height; without autoScroll, the end it opens at or scrollToEnd goes to is held while the content settles and comes, until the reader scrolls; a row replaced by another is not taken for a new message, which scrolled up to the first scrollAnchor message there at mount and left the end; its buttons take a finger at 44px, and hand the focus to the viewport once they have scrolled (the primitive blurs them and they go inert); with reduced motion they jump and fade without sliding; they float raised by shadow-float, which shows in dark, as shadow-md hardly did. Its buttons' words are labels; given a summary (the app's words on what waits below), a button becomes a pill with its label and a muted summary after an aria-hidden dot, truncated to fit, all of it in its name, announced only by the app. useMessageScrollerRelease ends a hold before an app scrolls the viewport itself, such as to a find match; without a provider it is a no-op. scrollToMessage(id, { highlight: true }) marks the message a moment where the reader was taken to it (a search's result, a link): the accent fading out over 1.2s (the theme's animate-highlight; held while marked with less motion); scrollToMessage(id, { part }) puts a part of it ([data-part-id], e.g. an AgentTurn's step, its folds opened by the app) 16px below the viewport's start once drawn, held there while what is above settles; an app's data-highlighted on a MessageScrollerItem does the same. It is a container (@container/message-scroller; not its viewport, as WebKit then misses the end it holds), so what is in it can take the room beside the column, as a Markdown table wider than the text does. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md). Its scroll buttons pop by the theme's motion-pop.

items.name: pagination
items.title: Pagination
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova pagination, fixed: Renders page links as links rather than as buttons. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: questionnaire
items.title: Questionnaire
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova questionnaire, fixed: the field's selection colours are its own (::selection), not its descendants' too, a rule every element of the page tried on every restyle; choices are light rows, not a stack of form fields: no border (but a keyboard focus's ring) and a grey row when checked; invalid, the choices and the Other field stay grey and the error is a line of an icon and red words under them; a choice's number key leads it in a hairline square and shows the choice, filled when checked, in place of the radio or checkbox; the Other field among the choices (QuestionnaireInput in QuestionnaireChoices) is one of their rows, not a form field, its placeholder in grey ("Something else…"), led by the key after the choices', which types in it, and grey like a checked choice once it has words. A single choice chosen (a click, its number key) goes on to the next question, not on the last nor by the arrow keys (advance); a field-only question, come to, is typed in; QuestionnaireNavigation is Previous, Skip, Next and Submit, each where it applies, and with onDecline a quiet Decline (QuestionnaireDecline, labels.decline) on every question, the way out of the whole questionnaire; QuestionnaireActions is a row, a Decline at its start; one question shows no progress. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: scroll-area
items.title: Scroll Area
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova scroll-area, fixed: Drops an unused React import that fails noUnusedLocals. A max-height on it holds: as tall as its content up to that, then it scrolls. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: slider
items.title: Slider
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova slider, fixed: takes getAriaValueText for its thumbs, so a slider of named steps (Low, Medium, High) says its value's name, not its number.

items.name: spinner
items.title: Spinner
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova spinner, fixed: Builds with Hugeicons, whose icon takes strokeWidth as a number only.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova switch, fixed: its size is in rem, as its thumb's is, so at a larger or smaller root font size the thumb stays inside it, on or off; at 16px it is as shadcn's. Off, it is a light track with a hairline and a grey thumb, quieter than on.

items.name: attachment
items.title: Attachment
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova attachment, fixed: an opt-in filled variant for a pasted-text chip, with a muted fill, no border, a 44px height, 8px corners and a regular-weight title; the container focus ring appears on keyboard focus only. Depends on the fixed button so installing it preserves that fix. The tile variant is a 64px square image tile with a covering image, rounded-lg corners and a subtle border; corner actions show on hover or focus and always on touch or error, the name stays available to screen readers, and tiles snap in a scrolling group. Running titles pause while out of view with use-shimmer-pause. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova button, fixed: in dark, an outline button is a hairline on the colour it is on (a page, a card, a dialog), as in light, without shadcn's bright input-coloured edge on a white tint. A disabled primary button is a muted one, not the primary half see-through (a grey that looks broken). Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: collapsible
items.title: Collapsible
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova collapsible, fixed: its content opens and closes in height and fades with it, in the theme's motion-size (at once where motion is reduced), clipped meanwhile.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova input, fixed: in dark, no fill, its border alone (3:1) outlining it, so it is not a grey slab on a card or a dialog. size="sm": 28px and 13px, beside a toolbar's or a composer's 28px buttons (36px on a phone, 16px text under 768px so iOS does not zoom); a number is still the native size. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: textarea
items.title: Textarea
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova textarea, fixed: in dark, no fill, its border alone (3:1) outlining it, so it is not a grey slab on a card or a dialog. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: native-select
items.title: Native Select
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova native select, fixed: in dark, no fill, its border alone (3:1) outlining it, so it is not a grey slab on a card or a dialog. Its selection's colours are its own (::selection), not its descendants' too, a rule every element of the page tried on every restyle. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: input-otp
items.title: Input OTP
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova input otp, fixed: in dark, no fill, its border alone (3:1) outlining it, so it is not a grey slab on a card or a dialog.

items.name: item
items.title: Item
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova item, fixed: ItemTitle's text, or its ItemLink, is one line ending in an ellipsis (a flex box takes no line clamp: a long title wrapped or ran past its column), as narrow as its column in a grid too (max-w-fit, not w-fit, whose fit-content made Firefox's and WebKit's grid columns as wide as the words); made a button (render={<button />}) it answers hover and a press as a link does, its words start-aligned, disabled faint. The current item (aria-current, e.g. the entry open beside a master–detail list, or a nav row), a selected one (aria-selected) or one marked data-active is on the hover's grey, kept. ItemGroup `columns` (n) lines its items' facts up in columns across them without a table: media where any item has it, content, then n columns (ItemMeta, a fact at an item's end: small, grey, tabular, at its column's end, or start with align="start", gone with hideBelow (md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl) where the group is narrower than that, the same in every row, leaving no space; ItemActions, at its column's end), each as wide as its widest, in each item's subgrid; on a phone, a list as without. size="compact": a long list's rows (devices, people, results), 32px as the sidebar's, 8px in, no outline whatever the variant, touching in an ItemGroup. ItemLink: an item's title as its link (or render={<button />}), stretched over the row, its actions above it, the row hovered where it is and its focus ring round the row; an Item render={<a />} is one link, hovered and focused the same. ItemGroupLabel heads a run of its items ("Today"), small and grey where their words start, lighter than a section's title (role="presentation" in a list, or render={<h3 />}). Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md). Its background answers the pointer by the theme's motion-hover. ItemDescription phoneOnly is a line only a phone shows (hidden from sm); the media and a compact row's padding count it only there, so on a desktop the icon stays centred on a one-line title. ItemTitle is no wider than its column (max-w-full), so a part of it cut short (truncate) is cut there, not over the next column. ItemMedia variant="number": a row's number on a 20px round grey mark, its digits of one width, so titles start on one line from 1 to 12.

items.name: drawer
items.title: Drawer
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova drawer, fixed: the grab handle is the 36x5 bar drawn (shadcn's is 96x4), and the overlay is a flat scrim, without the blur of the page behind it. From the bottom it is clear of the home indicator; DrawerContent's size is default, tall (to 1rem under the status bar) or full; on a short screen its footer's buttons are side by side. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md). Its overlay and popup move together by the theme's motion-slide (400ms on --ease-slide; a release a share of it by the swipe's strength), one curve where they had two.

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova tabs, fixed: Passes orientation to Base UI, so vertical tabs take ArrowUp and ArrowDown. The default list has a hairline round it and the active tab a hairline edge and a faint shadow, without shadcn's bright border in dark. Only the line variant has the line under its tab, so a list scrolling sideways does not scroll down too. TabsList `rule` (with variant="line"): the list across its container on a hairline rule, the current tab's underline over it, the tabs as wide as their words from its start. Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: toggle-group
items.title: Toggle Group
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova toggle-group, fixed: Passes orientation to Base UI, so vertical groups take ArrowUp and ArrowDown; in dark, a pressed item is a step lighter than a hovered one (both were bg-muted, hardly off the background). Its spacing on the 4px module (docs/grid.md).

items.name: trace
items.title: Trace
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova trace, fixed: Keeps pending and description text at 4.5:1 contrast, marks a failed line in greys, by weight, not red, and leaves its fold's title untinted, and a fold's title and content at its rows' size (text-sm); a line's description is its result, smaller, at the line's end, so results line up in a column; with reduced motion a fold opens and its chevron turns at once. Running titles pause while out of view with use-shimmer-pause.

items.name: use-highlighted-code
items.title: Use Highlighted Code
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova use-highlighted-code (used by code-block), fixed: the highlighter builds with exactOptionalPropertyTypes; code's tokens are classes by kind (code-keyword, code-string, code-number, code-function, code-type, code-tag, code-property, code-comment) coloured by the theme's variables, so a change of scheme or tone colours nothing again: in colour by default, each 4.5:1 or more on the page, cards, muted surfaces, the sidebar and a line's tint in either scheme, in greys under data-code-tone="graphite" (CodeBlock's tone; keywords bold, strings lighter, comments italic); some 70 languages, each loaded when first used, and registerLanguages for an app's own (a loader and other names for it); terminal output keeps ANSI colours at 4.5:1, dimmed text (2m) a lighter step that still is, not Shiki's half opacity; a token's bold, italic, underline and strikethrough show.

items.name: use-fold
items.title: Use Fold
items.description: Whether a part of a conversation is open: what the app's rule says for it as it is now (open while a tool runs, closed once it is done) until the reader opens or closes it; FoldProvider keeps the reader's choices by key, also when the part unmounts and mounts again. FoldFindable tells folds a conversation find is open (useFoldFindable); FoldFindText is a closed fold's text meanwhile, hidden until found, opening the fold when found.

items.name: use-follow-end
items.title: Use Follow End
items.description: Keeps a scrolling element, such as a code block of command output, at its end while its content grows, until the reader scrolls away (wheel, touch, keyboard or scrollbar); back at the end it follows again.

items.name: use-overflow
items.title: Use Overflow
items.description: Whether an element's content is taller or wider than it, kept as it and its content change: e.g. to make a scrolling region reachable by keyboard (tabIndex 0) only while it scrolls, as its arrow keys need it focused.

items.name: use-shimmer-pause
items.title: Use Shimmer Pause
items.description: Pauses every shimmer on the page while it is out of view and resumes it as it comes into view. One shared IntersectionObserver finds them by their animation, so no element needs a ref. The components that shimmer call it; an app's own shimmer is paused alongside them.

items.name: check-grid
items.title: Check Grid
items.description: A script that lists what in an app's own code is off agentui's grid (docs/grid.md), so its views keep to it as the components do: sizes and space on the 4px module, boxes from 96px on the 16px gutter, space a step of the scale (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128), glyphs 12, 14, 16 or 20px, type a named size on whole lines, a colour's opacity, a duration and a layer each one of their few, the viewport's one breakpoint (sm), and pixel constants and size props (`width={280}`) on the same rules. `node scripts/check-grid.ts [files or directories…]`, src/components and src/lib by default (.ts and .tsx); it exits 1 with what it found, for CI. A comment `grid: mark` above a line skips it (a mark, a dot, a handle), `grid: clear (…)` its space (room kept for a box), `motion:` its duration (a loop's or a stream's); a duration or an easing of a component's own (`duration-200`, `ease-[cubic-bezier(…)]`), not the theme's motion-hover, -fade, -size, -slide or -pop. Node 23.6 or later (it runs as TypeScript).

items.name: phone-sheet
items.title: Phone Sheet
items.description: What turns a menu's, a popover's or a select's popup into a sheet from the bottom on a phone (narrower than 640px), for dropdown-menu, context-menu, popover and select: the positioner pinned along the bottom of the screen, the popup across it up to 6rem below its top and clear of the home indicator, a scrim that closes it when tapped, a header with a handle that closes it when dragged down a quarter of its height or flicked, and an optional title, and rows 44px tall (`in-data-phone-sheet:`).

items.name: zoom
items.title: Zoom
items.description: The zoom steps viewers and the image editor share (10% to 2000%, a viewer's to 800%), and nextZoom: the next step in or out, at least a fifth larger or smaller.

items.name: use-mobile
items.title: Use Mobile
items.description: shadcn/ui's base-nova use-mobile, fixed: a phone is narrower than 640px, Tailwind's `sm`, not 768px (a foldable or a tablet has the desktop's layout); and it reads the media query with useSyncExternalStore instead of setting state in an effect.

items.name: virtual-list
items.title: Virtual List
items.description: A long list that renders only the items near the view, measuring each as it renders and again when it changes height; scrolls to an item by its key whether or not it is rendered, and keeps its heights while hidden. Built on TanStack Virtual.

items.name: virtual-grid
items.title: Virtual Grid
items.description: Items in columns, too many to render all: a grid of rows, or masonry (each item in the shortest column, as tall as it is, so pictures of any shape are whole). As many columns as fit, up to 12 as many as divide 12 (2, 3, 4 or 6: on the 12-column grid); heights measured, fractions too, and laid out again as a width, a font size or an image changes. Scrolls to and focuses an item by its key, asks for the next page near the end, keeps its place while hidden, and the arrow keys move between items by where they are, past those the app skips (skip).

items.name: viewer
items.title: Viewer
items.description: The skeleton of a thing open in a panel, e.g. a file: a toolbar above of islands with no line under them, the path's and one per group of tools (ViewerTools, each ViewerToolGroup an island of its own: a pill 36px high on the page's colour with a hairline and a faint shadow, a step lighter than the panel in dark, its buttons 28px; a lone tool a round island) (the path's folders folded into a menu where they have no room, the path on a row of its own over the tools where its name would be cut short of 6rem, a name cut keeping its extension) (back, its path as a breadcrumb or the app's start in their place, none where a tab names it, its own tools, the app's, add to chat, download, a menu of the app's), its content to the edges, and a status bar below (controls at the start, facts at the end), or an action bar (ViewerActionBar: what the actions act on, small, then the app's buttons, e.g. Discard and Commit); a frame whose toolbar would hold its path alone may go without one. Its parts compose any viewer; ViewerFrame lays them out from props, ViewerFrame is one row above in a panel and over the window alike (its path or `start`, the kind's own `lead` such as compare; its `zoom`, tools, the app's actions, add to chat, download, More with its facts at the top where the kind has no status bar, `statusBar={false}`), the content to the edges, and a floating bar of ways to change it at the content's foot (ViewerEditBar: a handle to drag it aside by, the kind's own such as an image's marking, then the app's `edits`, ViewerEditButton's icon and word, the icon alone where the viewer is under 24rem; gone with none). ViewerZoom is a toolbar's percent (a menu of Fit, in, out and the steps) or a status bar's zoom with Fit (its value a menu of the steps and Fit; in and out a step at least a fifth larger or smaller, so one from a fitted size is never a few percent), ViewerFrameEnd gives a frame's surroundings tools at the end of its toolbar (as ViewerOverlay's close), ViewerFrameTitlebar makes its toolbar the window's top row (as ViewerOverlay's: as tall as an AgentApp's titlebar, past the window's own buttons or --viewer-titlebar-start, dragging the window but by its controls; its name, its facts after it, quieter, not in More, then lead, the surroundings' tools at its end) and its tools islands under the content, as a photo app's (ways to change it, in place of the floating bar, then the zoom, tools, actions, add to chat, download and More; on two rows where they have no room on one), ViewerMenu a tool that opens a menu (More, or one of its own icon, as wide as its items), ViewerFilter a filter of its bars, ViewerFind a find bar (floating over the content, or a bar's field) with its count and the previous and next match, and ViewerUnsupported says a file has no preview. Buttons named by tooltips, a finger's place on touch screens. ViewerFrame takes position ({ index, count }), onPrevious and onNext for the app's others: round buttons by the content's sides (none at the ends) and "3 / 7" at its foot (labels.previous, next, among); ViewerSiblings draws them over any relative content.

items.name: viewer-overlay
items.title: Viewer Overlay
items.description: A viewer over the whole window, e.g. a conversation's image, as a dialog: to the window's edges, one surface (no inset, corners or card in it). The app's viewer (a MediaViewer, or any ViewerFrame) fills it, its toolbar the window's top row (ViewerFrameTitlebar): as tall as an AgentApp's titlebar (--agent-app-titlebar, else 44px), past the window's own buttons (--agent-app-titlebar-inset), dragging the window but by its controls ([data-titlebar], app-region: drag; a host that drags it itself does so on a pointerdown there whose target is not a control); the viewer's name at its start, its facts after it, quieter (not in More, which is there only for the app's menu), then its lead (an image's versions and compare); at its end "Open in side panel" (where the app has a panel to move it to) and close (its own row with the overlay's label where the viewer has no toolbar). The viewer's tools are islands at the middle of its foot, over the composer and never over the image: marking (a mode whose tools, Clear marks and the send come after it) and the app's edits, then the zoom with the viewer's and the app's tools, add to chat, download and More; on two rows where they have no room on one. A strip of the conversation's images at the start, under the row (even of one; a placeholder for one with no thumbnail yet, the app loading it when it is picked, a spinner while `loading`) picking the one shown, its current one ringed and kept in view, gone on a phone; round buttons to the one before and after by the viewer's sides, with a mouse while it points at the viewer or one has focus, always under a finger and on a phone (the app gives its viewer no previous and next of its own); past a phone's status bar; and the app's composer under it, to ask about what is shown while it is. ← → go to the one before and after, where focus is not in a field, a menu or a slider.

items.name: files-viewer
items.title: Files Viewer
items.description: A folder's files in a viewer, as a file manager has them, four ways: a tree of rows with when each changed and its size, a description after a name, a status letter after a changed file's, ignored ones dimmed; a grid of thumbnails (images' own, the rest their type's icon) with a caption and a badge; columns of folder after folder with the picked file's preview, folding away with no room; and a gallery of the picked file large over a strip. Sorted by any column, or in the app's order; in the app's groups under headings. One picked, the arrow keys moving it as each view has them, Enter to open; a filter by name keeps the folders on the way open; the filter takes the path's place in the toolbar, and the app's own search's results are a flat list, each with where it is, how many said in the field. Search selects the first available result, shows its Open hint, and keeps focus in the field while Up and Down move selection and Enter opens it. The field replaces the search tool; its clear button closes it. The status bar shows the search folder, keyboard hints and results shown out of the supplied item count, preserving app controls and details. Only the rows in view are drawn, in the list and in each column. Folders loading, the files, previews and what opening does are the app's. A row may carry what a change adds and removes (+n −n) after its status. Disabled entries remain visible for context, skip selection and opening, and are passed by the keys in every view. The list leaves out a Modified or Size column no loaded file has; start puts the app's control in the path's place. The count prop optionally counts only the filtered top level for item and changed facts, preserving search result totals. levelFilter filters one folder's enabled files by name prefix, as a typed path's last segment does, driven by the app's input with no field opened: the other levels stay whole, the status bar says n of m items, a level with none says No matches; the toolbar's filter, while it has text, takes precedence. tree={false} shows a flat top-level list; openOn="click" opens on tap, onUp asks for the parent, and loading shows a spinner while files arrive. header={false} drops the list's column header and filter={false} the toolbar's filter; count can name one folder to count. A disabled entry takes no focus unless all are; one column alone keeps a column's width. Rows are 44px tall under a coarse pointer. It has no fill of its own: it takes the surface it sits on, a dialog's or a card's. Columns resize at each border with a fine pointer: drag, arrow keys or Home/End; double click or Enter resets. Widths by depth use columnWidths/defaultColumnWidths/onColumnWidthsChange; the fit count follows.

items.name: folder-picker
items.title: Folder Picker
items.description: A folder chooser built on FilesViewer, in a dialog or an embedded panel (autoFocus: its path field focused as it is shown, as the dialog's). Columns or a tree, with a path field, places and optional folder creation; files hidden or disabled for context. Enter goes into a folder, Cmd or Ctrl with Enter chooses it; Escape restores an edited path or cancels folder creation before closing the dialog. On a phone it fills the screen and shows one folder at a time, a flat list: a tap goes into a folder, the breadcrumb goes back up, Choose picks the folder shown, and the places are a select standing for the place's root at the start of the breadcrumb (chosen again, back to the root). On a larger screen the path field sits in the browser's toolbar, the only location and filter: no breadcrumb, no toolbar filter; the places a list with their icons. A folder with no path leaves the field empty with its placeholder. The count is the level being picked in. The dialog's footer is whole on a phone, above the home indicator. The tree, loading, paths, places, creating folders and whether a folder can be chosen are the app's. Loads deduplicate hover and focus prefetch with abort signals and independent loading columns. The typed path steers the browser: its last segment filters the folder typed into (only that level, VS Code style), n of m items in the status bar, No matches where none do; the first match is selected with inline completion, Up/Down cycle the filtered folders, Tab steps in, and with no match the typed folder itself is selected. Columns resize on a larger screen, with widths passed through to FilesViewer.

items.name: media-viewer
items.title: Media Viewer
items.description: An image, a video or a recording in a viewer, by its kind, in a viewer's frame. An image: on a checkerboard where it has transparent parts (found as it loads), flat (no corners, no shadow), fitted to the edges or zoomed (its percent in the toolbar, a menu of Fit, in, out and the steps; Ctrl or Cmd with the wheel, + - and 0; under fingers a pinch about its middle as far as they go, not the page's, a double tap fitting it or zooming in to 200% there, a swipe across it fitted going to the one before or after, with its marking tools too while not marking), copied as a PNG, no status bar under it (its size and the app's facts at the top of More, compare at the toolbar's start), fitted and its size said before it loads where the app gives its width and height, its thumbnail over its placeholder standing in at its size till it is drawn; its versions in a strip of thumbnails under it picking the one shown (in a ViewerFrameTitlebar, a menu at the toolbar's start instead, the one shown in words), which is compared with the original by a line dragged between them (the facts saying when each was); one of the app's images, back and forth by buttons at its sides and the arrow keys, where it is ("30 of 60") in the facts, the comparison flat too, its divider and grip following the theme background; its areas brushed, circled or framed and sent to the app (onMark, markImages making the mask and an annotated copy), marks or a mask of what changed shown, its marking tools in the viewer's floating bar of edits, before the app's `edits` (on a ViewerFrameTitlebar's island under it instead, Mark first, then while marking its tools, Clear marks and the send there, not by the marks) ("Mark an area" in words, its icon alone where the viewer is narrow), drawn as when only looked at (no checkerboard for an opaque one, fitted to the edges, flat; a click zooms in a step). A video: on black, its controls over it in any theme (play, time, a seek bar showing the frame under the pointer, sound, full screen), speed and loop below with its size and length. A recording: its title, a waveform of the app's peaks to seek on (a slider by keys too), and a transcript line by line, the line being said lit, each going there; speed, loop and copying the transcript below. Space plays and pauses, the arrows go 5 seconds; what cannot be shown or played says so. crossOrigin (e.g. use-credentials) and mediaProps give the app the element, to go to a time, and its events. Its image editor and comparison are its own files. Its position, onPrevious and onNext are the frame's (position { index, count }), for any kind: the buttons by its sides and "3 / 7" at its foot; an image's arrows and swipe go to them too.

items.name: pdf-viewer
items.title: PDF Viewer
items.description: A PDF in a viewer. With the app's rendered pages (e.g. PDF.js's canvas and text layer): a rail of the pages, the pages one under another, page by page, zoom with Fit to the width, and a find bar (Ctrl or Cmd+F) that marks what it finds in the pages' text with the CSS Custom Highlight API, no elements added. With only a file: the browser's own PDF viewer in a frame, told the page and zoom by its address.

items.name: table-viewer
items.title: Table Viewer
items.description: A table in a viewer, e.g. a CSV file (parseCsv reads RFC 4180): row numbers, each column's type under its name (numbers found, to the end), only the rows in view drawn. A cell picked by a click or the keys (arrows, Page Up and Down, Home and End); the status bar says which and a column of numbers' sum; filtered by text, sorted by the picked column, and the picked cell given to the app by @.

items.name: terminal-viewer
items.title: Terminal Viewer
items.description: Terminals in a viewer, a tab per process with a live dot while it runs: its output with its ANSI colours, following its end while it comes; Stop, Clear and Send output to chat below, with the app's words on it at the end.
